subject.title: fix(auth-profiles): import legacy auth-profiles.json into SQLite store on load

question: Should stranded legacy credentials be recovered through the existing doctor/migration boundary, or should legacy JSON become a temporary credential authority during every runtime load?
rationale: Both choices affect credential consent, stale-secret authority, upgrade behavior, cleanup, and the explicit SQLite-only storage contract; repository policy favors doctor-owned migration, but the exact automatic versus user-confirmed recovery UX requires owner intent.

options.title: Doctor-owned recovery
options.body: Keep runtime SQLite-only and relocate the recovery into a startup-triggered or clearly surfaced doctor migration with backup, verification, complete field preservation, and source cleanup.

options.title: Temporary runtime compatibility
options.body: Explicitly approve the legacy file as a time-bounded runtime credential source, document precedence and consent behavior, and add a concrete removal migration and expiry plan.

options.title: Coordinate the migration cluster
options.body: Pause this PR until the canonical issue and related doctor migration PRs can be resolved as one coherent upgrade-recovery design.

recommendation.title: Doctor-owned recovery
recommendation.body: Keep runtime SQLite-only and relocate the recovery into a startup-triggered or clearly surfaced doctor migration with backup, verification, complete field preservation, and source cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: The SQLite auth-store refactor established the current canonical-store and doctor-migration boundary that this decision would change.
